description:
FILED AND FIXED s473h (Opus, 2026-09-08), pre-existing at a9f2a264.  Found
while wiring #1529 (the synthetic $ENV{_PCL_RUNTIME_} entry), because that
change made `keys %ENV` and `scalar(%ENV)` have to agree.

PROBE (scratch/s473h/probe/m10c.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs PCL at a9f2a264):

    my $k = scalar(keys %ENV);
    my $s = scalar(%ENV);
    print "keys=$k scalar=$s\n";

    perl   keys=78 scalar=78
    PCL    keys=78 scalar=HASH(0x1)

Same for `scalar(%INC)`.

THE CAUSE.  Since #736 the %ENV and %INC markers ARE the hash â every hash
primitive knows the symbol.  `p-scalar` did not: its `hash-table-p` arm could
not see a marker, so the symbol fell through to the catch-all `(t v)` and was
stringified as a hash REFERENCE.  Perl 5.26+ gives a plain `%hash` in scalar
context its KEY COUNT.

THE FIX: one arm beside the hash-table one, counting through `p-keys` â the
ONE walk of those two containers (#736, rule 11) â so `scalar(%ENV)` and
`keys %ENV` cannot disagree.  `scalar(\%ENV)` is unchanged and still the
reference (the arm carries the same `(not (p-box-p val))` guard the
hash-table arm has).

GUARDS: Pl/t/pcl-runtime-env-01.t rows 10-12 (count agrees with keys for
%ENV; the same for %INC; the `\%ENV` negative), inverse-verified â 10 and 11
fail on the a9f2a264 extraction, 12 passes there and must keep passing.

=== DONE (s473h) ===
subject: FIXED s473h: `scalar(%ENV)` / `scalar(%INC)` answered HASH(0x1) instead of the key count -- p-scalar had no arm for the %ENV/%INC MARKER, which IS the hash (#736)
